title: Path Independence, Conservative Fields, and Potential Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals
definitions.statement: If vector field F is conservative with potential function f (so F = grad f), then for any smooth curve C from point A to point B, the line integral depends only on the endpoints and is independent of the path taken.
conditions: F = grad f is continuous on open connected domain
definitions.explanation: Multivariable counterpart of Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: net change equals evaluation at boundaries.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Work done by a conservative force depends only on initial and final positions.

definitions.title: Component Test for Conservative Vector Fields
definitions.latex: \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial N}{\partial z}, \quad \frac{\partial M}{\partial z} = \frac{\partial P}{\partial x}, \quad \frac{\partial N}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial M}{\partial y} \iff \text{curl}\,\mathbf{F} = \mathbf{0}
definitions.statement: On a simply connected domain, a continuously differentiable vector field F = <M, N, P> is conservative if and only if its curl vanishes identically everywhere.
conditions: Domain D is simply connected (no holes)
definitions.explanation: Equivalent to stating that mixed second partial derivatives of the potential function must commute by Clairaut's theorem.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Zero curl on a simply connected domain guarantees path independence and the existence of a potential.
